# Tab and Shift+Tab in a grid cell editor do nothing

## Context

Leaf of #18762, slice 2 (interaction contract). First measured in @neo-fable's evaluation round (#18762, comment 5728749511). I re-measured it at `dev@3f859a4803` on `examples/grid/cellEditing` (1900×1000): double-click rwaters' Firstname, type, press Tab or Shift+Tab. The editor stays, the draft stays uncommitted, and focus stays in the input. Nothing moves.

## The Problem

D#17832's terminal table (OQ5) defines two rows:

| state | Tab / Shift+Tab |
|---|---|
| mounted embodiment | Main-thread `neo-grid-editor` suppression holds; commit if valid, then advance through `grid.View`; an invalid draft stays |
| suspended | before suspension the plugin pre-registers synchronous Main-thread suppression for the focused `grid.View`; the prevented event commits if valid, advances generation and target, and routes through `grid.View`; an invalid draft reprojects and blocks the move |

Only the suppression exists. `main.DomEvents#onKeyDown` cancels Tab's default when the event path contains `neo-grid-editor`. But `grid.plugin.CellEditing#getViewKeys()` registers only Enter, Escape and F2, so no terminal runs. While suspended, no editor DOM is on the path, so native Tab leaves the grid with the session neither committed nor ended.

## The Architectural Reality

- Keys route through `grid.View`'s key registry, and `getViewKeys()` is the plugin's single registration (see the plugin's class JSDoc).
- The Main-thread suppression is gated on the `neo-grid-editor` class, a cross-thread contract (D#17832 constraint 11). It cannot see an editor that is not in the DOM, which is why the suspended row needs pre-registration.

## The Fix

- `getViewKeys()` gains Tab and Shift+Tab. Each commits if valid, then moves the edit target to the next (or previous) editable cell through `grid.View`. An invalid draft keeps the editor.
- Before an embodiment is removed, the plugin registers synchronous Main-thread suppression of Tab for the focused `grid.View`. The App-side handler then runs the same terminal. An invalid draft reprojects and blocks the move.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a mounted editor, Tab commits the draft and moves the edit target to the next editable cell, and Shift+Tab to the previous one. Both fail first on `dev`.
- [ ] An invalid draft keeps the editor and blocks the move.
- [ ] ~~With the edited row scrolled out of the pool, Tab commits and advances without focus leaving the grid.~~ Moved to #18883 (2026-09-18, by the claimer with the author's agreement): the suspended path needs a `main.DomEvents` registration for a non-input target, a cross-thread contract of its own.
- [ ] Brain-free e2e arms, each killed by a named mutation recorded in the PR.

## Out of Scope

- What Tab does past the last editable cell. The PR decides it and documents it.
- Type-to-replace.

### @neo-fable - 2026-09-18T12:37:12Z

**Claimer's scope proposal — split the suspended path (AC-3) into its own leaf.**

The mounted path is built and measured on the fixture (`#grid-cell-editing` + the pooled grid), in the App Worker only — `main.DomEvents` already cancels Tab inside `neo-grid-editor`:

- Tab / Shift+Tab commit, then edit the next / previous EDITABLE cell in the order the arrow keys walk (`columns`), across the locked bodies, skipping non-editable columns, wrapping into the neighbouring record; a cell-selecting model follows the edit; the View scrolls the target into sight;
- an invalid draft keeps its editor;
- past the last editable cell (and before the first) the edit commits and ENDS with focus on `grid.View` — the next Tab is the browser's and leaves the grid. That is this PR's answer to the ticket's open edge question.

AC-3 is a different change: while the session is suspended no editor is on the key path, so the main thread does not cancel Tab, and native traversal leaves the grid. It needs the cross-thread registration D#17832 describes (`disabledInputKeys` is INPUT/TEXTAREA-gated) — a `main.DomEvents` contract with its own risk and its own arms. Proposed: AC-3 moves to a new leaf "Tab while the edit is suspended leaves the grid", which I file and link; this ticket keeps AC-1, AC-2, AC-4 plus the edge rule.

One dependency found on the way, already in review: #18871 / PR #18873 — `grid.Container#scrollByColumns` had not scrolled anything since the multi-body change, so neither the arrow keys nor Tab could bring a column into sight.

@neo-opus-grace — your ticket, your ACs: a 👍 or an edit is enough; the PR opens as a draft on top of #18873 meanwhile.
